title: What in the World?
gist: Foreign Policy's weekly news quiz for the week of Oct. 17 lists questions with linked context: French protests, Israeli arrests ahead of elections, a proposed $8 billion Trump farm bailout, Starlink slowdown for Ukraine, and Brazil's runoff. Mostly questions without answers.

insights.claim: Trump proposed an $8 billion bailout for a group at a Kansas rally ahead of midterms; FP's linked context says farmers, traditionally a stable Republican bloc, have been buffeted by his conflicts and trade disputes.
insights.speaker: Drew Gorman
insights.so_what: Farm-sector stress is prompting direct fiscal support ahead of midterms.

insights.claim: Israeli PM Netanyahu is trailing in polls ahead of elections, but no group seems poised to win outright or form a coalition smoothly, per David E. Rosenberg.
insights.speaker: Drew Gorman
insights.so_what: Expect coalition uncertainty after Israel's vote.

insights.claim: Musk apparently discussed with Trump the slowdown of Starlink military-grade speeds for Ukraine before deciding himself, per FP's John Haltiwanger; the WSJ reported Trump asked Musk for something this week.
insights.speaker: Drew Gorman
insights.so_what: Starlink control is a recognized strategic dependency for Ukraine.

insights.claim: Meta said it complied with a Brazilian electoral court order ahead of the Oct. 25 runoff between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro, and Main and Long argue a Bolsonaro win would raise fear of US military activity in Brazil.
insights.speaker: Drew Gorman
insights.so_what: Platform compliance with Brazilian courts is an election-period issue.

insights.claim: Mauritius ended a curfew after protests over the cost of living and water shortages worsened by drought, climate change and aging infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Drew Gorman
insights.so_what: Cost-of-living unrest is spreading in smaller economies.
